review_text_raw:
I'm [i]really[/i] glad to have a game like this where the story isn't just "surveillance bad".

The mechanics are good though sometimes it can be hard to scan things even when you know what to scan. Special ways to solve problems are generally only used once and can be decently complex and fun because of that. They're usually a refreshing change and can be [i]incredibly[/i] intense. I just wish certain things would be randomized between attempts.

Now for the story. Like I said, I'm very glad it didn't go for the usual story this type of game attracts. It's a fairly decent plot with likeable, well voiceacted characters and let's you figure out certain things early without being utterly obvious.

The problem is the ending. The rest will be in spoilers, though I'm not gonna say anything specific. This is basically just for people that are really adverse to any kind spoiler, no matter how small.

[spoiler]The story is very good at making you think that your choices matter; though they ultimate do not. The stakes feel astronomical in multiple situations, but turn out to be utterly meaningless in the end. And there's no easy way to say this, but:

The ending sucks. Ruining the rest of the game levels of bad.

For starters, there is only one, even if it might seem you'd have at least 2 paths to go down. On top of that it is abrupt, doesn't make any sense and the person responsible for said ending was probably meant to seem really intimidating and constantly in control. This is not the case and the person ends up looking incredibly incompetent and only seems to succeed because everyone else is even more of an idiot.

I can not overstate enough that the entire game was fun - only for the entire mood to be ruined at the end, seemingly just to set up a sequel that could've easily focused on a different conspiracy. I genuinely do not know how it was fumbled this badly.[/spoiler]

review_text_raw:
****SOME SMALL SPOILERS****

It was enjoyable to play as the music and the visuals were good. But in terms of story building it lacked quite a bit. The whole game kind of treats you like an idiot. It's very hand-holding, do this do that. There is some problem solving and some puzzles here and there that made it more challenging but mostly the puzzles look like this: this file needs a password to enter, how do you find a password? ask Hal! Hal what's the password? here it is: 123456. I'm in! H4CK3R MAN!

Also there is only one ending, so it doesn't feel like your choices matter that much.
Another criticism of the story is the beginning, it starts with a major spoiler of the whole mystery. You can kind of guess the whole plot twist because of it. It was super obvious. I feel like the beginning wasn't necessary and would have made me appreciate the story more.

The things it did well are the more stressful and challenging puzzles. For example the bomb diffusing was fun. And the floppy disk code finding was good. That's all I can think of right now. The carDB was used I think only once and then never again. I wish there was just a bit more complexity. Anyways, not the worst game. I wouldn't refund it and I don't regret buying it or playing it. Just wished for more

[h1]Meh[/h1]

This is one of the games where I wish there would be a "Meh" option.

I plaid the Demo and was looking forward to the games release as this sort of "operate and solve puzzles from your PC" ones are much to my liking. 

Unfortunately the game itself was quite linear, very few and quite easy puzzles and the story sort of foreseeable. 

Choices matter a little bit, but as soon as you had your play through you will only see the results at the very end. There is no save function, no chapters, so if you wanna try out other choices you will have to go through the exact same stuff another time - which is a bit boring as the story is very linear.

Perfect game if you want to click a few buttons every once in a while and not think to much.

review_text_raw:
I'm only giving this a thumbs down because I believe this is marketed incorrectly. I loved the game for what it is, a visual novel. But this is not necessarily a detective game, and I'd argue not even really investigative.
The game follows one story line, and kind of fools you into thinking your choices matter when they really don't. For example, I attempted every dialogue option to not work with HAL, but that didn't matter, I had to work with them anyway.
The tools used are awesome; facial recognition, Human Database, lab analysis. But we only use some of these things once or a few times at most.
Don't get me wrong, the story is fantastic, and I genuinely loved my time with it. I agree with a lot of the other reviews that this should be way longer, but overall, I think the game is marketed incorrectly which is where I can't recommend it. I, and it seems a lot of others, went into this with the idea I would be solving multiple cases, using the technology multiple times, maybe even an endless mode where there's multiple variations of possible cases. 
I do think it's a great game, the immersion into the FDI computer is fantastic, the art style/graphics are perfect, everything ran smoothly. I mean genuinely top marks across (most of) the board. But it did leave me wanting more, I really dislike that we only used some of the tools once, and my choices didn't matter. All that being said, I absolutely would purchase another game from this dev.

review_text_raw:
I would classify this as a short narrative game with very light puzzles.

PUZZLES
A majority of the puzzles are signposted and obvious, and they all give a tutorial vibe. The game will teach you how to solve a particular type of puzzle, but then that type of puzzle is never visited again.

There were two puzzles that weren't, but these felt frustrating as:
- the first one had VERY confusing wording and used terms that were not explained ("tickable" being the word I got stuck on)
- the second one you needed to brute force a solution, which is never fun nor rewarding

NARRATIVE
For a mystery game, the final twist was basically shouted at the beginning of the game and I guessed it within the first 5 minutes. All of the cases pertain to the main mystery (no side missions to divert your attention). When you know the secret right away, it's hard to feel motivated to continue playing.

In the end, I felt it was a shallow, predictable, and simple game. It has good bones, but needed a lot more time in the oven

If a sequel does come along, or this team makes a similar game, I hope they:
- Include more puzzles
- Not make the ending obvious
- Playtest all the puzzles to make sure that things are easily understood and enjoyable (without losing the theme)
- Add in some red herrings/busywork 
- Show off their systems! Similar to a Hypnospace Outlaw or The Roottrees are Dead, have us use the mechanics more than once before moving on to a completely different thing. I would have loved to do more searching, scrubbing, etc in the game but didn't have enough opportunities outside each mechanic's single puzzle.

I was expecting a puzzle game, solving cases and helping on-site agents, but I instead get babysitted by a hacker, in a very anti-immersive "game" (cause it feels more like a story that I click to advance than a game) filled with conspiracy stuff.
None of what you do matters, none of your choices matter, you can't fail, which means you never win.

If you expected a game like a 911 operator but to help on-site FBI agents, that's not it, it's just a game-shaped story.
